transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Priya Karan (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (NexaHealth Head of ML), Mark Chen (Eng Manager), Liam O'Neill (CTO), Asha Patel (DevOps)
Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/poc/nexahealth/benchmarks (spreadsheet)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call and then we'll jump into the numbers. we only have 45 minutes so we'll try to keep tight.
[00:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here. ready.
[00:12] Mark: Mark, yep.
[00:14] Liam: Liam on.
[00:16] Asha: Asha here.
[00:20] Sofia: Cool, so agenda - recap last week's tuning (batching and quant), share latest benchmarks vs your baseline provider \"CloudAI\" and agree on follow-ups. Ethan, want to start with the headline numbers?
[00:30] Ethan: Yeah sure. So we ran the same benchmark harness you provided - 512 token average context, mixture of short and long prompts, 5 minute warmup then 10 minute recorded run. We compared Redwood configured with int8 quant, batch size 16, prefix caching enabled to the baseline (default provider config).
[00:50] Ethan: Headline: p50 latency Redwood ~110ms vs baseline ~220ms; p95 Redwood ~360ms vs baseline ~980ms. Throughput: Redwood sustained ~380 requests/sec at target quality vs baseline ~210 rps before p95 climbed. That's with concurrency of 64 client threads.
[01:15] Dr. Priya Rao: Those p95 numbers are ... impressive. Did you keep exact same sequence lengths and tokenization? We need apples-to-apples.
[01:22] Ethan: Yes we used your tokenizer and the same prompt set, there is small variance in how providers handle padding but we normalized by measuring tokens/sec not just raw latency. The spreadsheet has warm vs cold run tabs - cold first-run is higher for both as expected.
[01:38] Mark: Quick Q - what's the cost delta per 1M tokens roughly? We saw Redwood looked slightly higher on a pure per-token compute assumption earlier.
[01:45] Sofia: Good point. The current run shows Redwood compute cost slightly lower when you include caching and higher utilization - effective cost per 1M tokens is about 12% lower on our test profile. We'll include line-items in the sheet.
[01:58] Liam: On caching - can you explain the prefix caching behavior? We have a lot of repeated preambles in our prompts.
[02:05] Ethan: Sure. Prefix KV caching stores the key/value for repeated prefix tokens on the serving side so for repeated prompts you avoid re-computing the same attention layers. On our bench it reduced compute by about 30% for the repeated subset, which drove the throughput up and cost down. There was a small effect on p95 cold starts though.
[02:28] Dr. Priya Rao: Any differences in quality after quantization? We care about hallucination and exact numeric outputs for our clinical notes.
[02:35] Ethan: We did a quick f1/accuracy style comparison on your eval set. int8 quant reduced latency ~18% with negligible delta on the metrics you care about - for the LLM family you're running (decoder-only medium), the quality delta was within noise. We'll run extended evals if you want.
[02:52] Priya Karan: (inaudible) quantisization, quanti-? there was one prompt where the punctuation moved but overall stable.
[03:00] Mark: Can you surface p50/p95 across sequence length buckets? Our traffic has a long right tail.
[03:06] Ethan: Absolutely - the sheet has 0-128, 129-512, 513-1024 buckets. For 513-1024 p95 Redwood ~980ms but still better than baseline's 1.6s p95. We also included throughput curves at different concurrencies.
[03:25] Asha: Security question - for Private deployment, do you support bring-your-own-KMS and HIPAA BAAs? We need that to move forward.
[03:33] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and we can enable a HIPAA BAA for covered workflows. We'll trigger security to join the deep-dive next week.
[03:44] Liam: Network - how much egress between our VPC and the serving nodes? We want to avoid large data movement.
[03:50] Ethan: If you run Private in your VPC, model weights stay in the private cluster; only telemetry and metrics (optional) go to control plane. For hosted routes there's standard egress; we'll get Asha the network diagram.
[04:05] Dr. Priya Rao: On latency: can you break down where time is spent? Is it model runtime, kernel overhead, or network?
[04:12] Ethan: Good question. Roughly 70% of the token latency is model runtime (kernel conv and attention), 20% is framing/transport, 10% is orchestration overhead. Our kernel selection and compilation pipeline helped reduce runtime compared to the baseline which appears to use older kernels. The per-token compute optimizations are the big delta.
[04:36] Mark: We had one outlier in your run at minute ~7 where p95 spiked to 1.6s even on Redwood, what's that?
[04:42] Ethan: That correlates with an autoscaler event in the test harness - a transient cold-start of a worker node. We can rerun with pinned capacity to show steady-state. Also the warmup behavior differs.
[04:55] Sofia: Ok let's call out tuning items: pin capacity for steady-state, increase batch size to 24 for higher throughput tests, and run an int8 sweep to confirm quality.
[05:05] Dr. Priya Rao: Can you also show a run with our highest-length prompts and 128 concurrency, we want to see tail behavior.
[05:10] Ethan: Yep we'll add that to the high-concurrency run.
[05:14] Asha: For compliance, will you provide SOC 2 Type II and encryption-at-rest docs?
[05:18] Sofia: Yes - we'll share security pack, SOC 2 report, and the HIPAA checklist. Expect links in the shared drive.
[05:26] (crosstalk)
[05:35] Liam: One more question on fallbacks: if dedicated capacity hits a limit, what happens?
[05:40] Priya Karan: There's smart routing - requests can failover to compatible variants or different region; Redwood can also route to a lower-cost model variant with fallback rules you set.
[05:52] Mark: How easy is model pinning and rollbacks? We have CI integration needs.
[05:56] Ethan: You can pin model versions per route, do canary rollouts and automatic fallback on quality regressions. We have a rollout API you can tie into your CI.
[06:07] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. Accepting the numbers so far but we'll need the extra runs before executive sign-off.
[06:12] Sofia: Understood. To recap - Redwood wins on p50/p95 and throughput in our tests, caching and quantization helped considerably. Actions: updated sheet, high-concurrency run, security deep-dive.
[06:22] Mark: Thanks - can you also add a slide comparing cost per effective request (after caching) vs raw token cost?
[06:27] Sofia: Yes will add a cost breakdown slide.
[06:30] Ethan: I'll kick off the stress test later today and upload logs.
[06:34] Asha: we'll pull network and KMS details and share.
[06:37] Sofia: Ok thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the security deep-dive.
[06:44] (meeting ends)
notes: Spreadsheet link in transcript; warm vs cold runs noted; recommend pinned capacity for steady-state tests. Some transcription artifacts: 'quantisization' and 'K-V cash' appear in auto transcript.
